title: review-map
description: The contract between the generator (/whydiff) and the viewer (templates/viewer.html). Files are addressed by repo-relative path — there are no synthetic ids.

lang.description: Report language (BCP-47: 'en', 'ru'…). The generator takes the chat conversation language; if it cannot be determined, 'en'. Controls both the content language (why/story/…) and the viewer interface language. The tool's source code and identifiers are always English.

attentionFiles.description: How many files need careful reading

intent.description: The tl;dr of the change in one sentence — what it does, so a reviewer gets the gist without opening a tab. Not the mechanics (that is story) or the risks (those are ops). Inline <b>/<code> allowed.

story.description: The causal chain, the default view. Steps are interleaved with "why" links (principle 4).

group.description: group id — sets the step color

files.description: Paths of the files involved in the step

link.description: A link between steps: WHY the next block exists

groups.description: Groups = review roles, not file types (principle 2).

role.description: What the reviewer should do: read (read carefully) | verify-pattern (check one pattern and the completeness of the list) | context (context, read first) | ops (deploy checklist) | spec (specification on request, may be collapsed) | plumbing (mechanics)

files.description: The key is a repo-relative path.

service.description: The file's logical scope — the viewer builds the tag panel from these: frontend / backend / api / mcp / devops / infra / docs / test… Required for every file; lowercase, consistent across the whole diff.

role.description: The file's role in the change, briefly

frag.description: Fragment for the inspector: [class, text], class: add|del|ctx

preview.description: 1–2 lines per card (principle 1: preview up front, text lazily)

embedFull.description: assemble.mjs will embed the file's full text from --repo

edges.description: [fromPath, toPath, title, description?] (principle 3). `title` is a SHORT label that rides on the connector line — a phrase of a few words ("records the refund row", "calls settlement after shipping"), never a sentence. `description` is optional: one or two sentences of the fuller reasoning, shown on hover; omit it when the title already says everything.

diagrams.description: Only where a control/data flow changes (principle 6). Diff-marked in a single graph (principle 7): added/removed/changed classes WITHOUT classDef — the color comes from the viewer's own tokens.

kind.description: er-diff — a mermaid erDiagram of data-schema changes; required when the diff contains migrations that change table structure

caption.description: One sentence: what is visible here

mermaid.description: In flowchart diagrams, file nodes are made clickable with the line `click <id> call whydiffOpen("<repo-relative path>")`; the path must exist in files (checked by validate.mjs).

files.description: Which files the drill-down leads to

pattern.description: Reference to a project convention: "the project does X, see Y"

fixed.description: Which assertions are now pinned down — in plain language

gaps.description: What is NOT covered — more valuable than a coverage percentage

userStories.description: What changed on the OUTSIDE, in the actor's language: stories reconstructed from the diff. The other sections are engineering — this one answers "what can a person now do, and what broke for them". An empty array is meaningful: "external behavior did not change" is information too (principle 5).

summary.description: 1–2 sentences: whether external behavior changed at all. For a purely internal change it must say so outright.

actor.description: Who acts: a user role, an operator, an external system. Only those visible in the diff — do not invent them.

story.description: "I can …, so that …" from the actor's point of view. No class, table or function names — those go in files.

status.description: Whether the diff actually delivers this story: delivered — yes; partial — works, but with a defect; broken — the code exists, but the path does not fire; regressed — it got WORSE on the outside than before. This is what turns the tab from documentation into a review tool.

why.description: What in the diff confirms it and what exactly gets in the way. For anything other than delivered, the cause and location must be named.

files.description: Diff files that deliver this story — drill-down. Checked by validate.mjs.

covered.description: Whether a test pins down this exact story. false is a notable signal for a money- or access-related story.

ops.description: Operational checklist. Empty lists are meaningful: "env did not change" is information too.

blastRadius.description: Depends on what changed, but is not in the diff.

generated.description: Which optional passes actually ran (standards|tests|stories). Written by merge.mjs from which agent files existed; the viewer offers a Generate button for the rest and appends here on demand. Absent on pre-lazy maps (viewer falls back to key presence).

manifest.description: Every file in the diff: [path, +, −, groupId, isNew]. Completeness is checked by a script against git diff --numstat (principle 5).

fullFiles.description: Populated by assemble.mjs from embedFull flags; not written by hand.
